rules: First matching row wins. `class` names the Reference-side member class; `under` requires an ancestor of that class; `mro_missing` admits an mro difference only when the Reference chain is the portal chain plus exactly those names; `scope` (constructions, scenes, or any by default) limits where a row applies and is checked for staleness. A behavior-note row is a deliberate, documented divergence. An open-bead row is a known bug: an open-bead row that matches nothing in its scope fails the diff, so a fixed bug forces its row out. A Behavior Note justifies a different outline, not an unbounded size or position, so every behavior-note or ADR row that covers bbox carries an `envelope`: {size_rel, center_abs} bounds each axis's extent to size_rel of the Reference's and its centre to center_abs scene units, or {bounded_by: ancestor} defers to the envelope of the `under` ancestor whose bbox contains it. A bbox outside a row's envelope falls through to later rows; an open-bead row may state its bug's measured magnitude as an envelope. A bbox no row admits is a difference that names the first envelope it broke (fm-5wq.45).

exclusions.reason: C-19: at the pin StringMobject.__init__ re-applies its white fill_color after color= reached SVGMobject, so Text(..., color=X) renders white. FrankenManim applies the requested color (BN-07). The row applies only where the Reference shows that default white.

C-19: at the pin Dot passes fill_color=DEFAULT_MOBJECT_COLOR and stroke_color=BLACK to Circle, masking the caller's color=; Dot(color=RED) is white with a black stroke. FrankenManim ranks color= above constructor defaults and an explicit channel above color= (fm-qead), so Dot(color=RED, fill_color=BLUE) keeps the blue fill the Reference also keeps and a red stroke where the Reference shows black. The row applies only where the Reference shows those defaults.

C-30: at the pin BackgroundRectangle.get_fill_color() returns Color(self.color), Mobject's default white, whatever the fill is. FrankenManim reports the rectangle's color, the constructor's color= (BN-07).

C-31: at the pin set_style writes rgba arrays into data only, so match_style is dropped on a point-less mobject. DashedVMobject's root keeps VMobject's defaults, and a VCube root keeps its own BLUE_D fill (SumOfTwoSquares: cube.match_style(square)). FrankenManim's root takes the source's style (BN-07). The classes name point-less roots only (dashes and faces are VMobject or Square), and the row applies only where the Reference shows those defaults.

Glyph outlines come from the bundled faces (BN-05), and SVG and CFF cubics go through the one error-bounded converter (BN-13), so point counts and positions of SVG-derived paths differ wherever scenes regroup them. Envelope: a regrouped glyph's box may differ by a quarter of its extent and move by a tenth of a unit (BN-05's sub-em shifts); a glyph inside a text ancestor falls through to that ancestor's bound.

The portal's Tex submobjects are every glyph, then every rule, then every drawn path, where the Reference keeps TeX's emission order (39 corpus scenes: equal glyph counts, a t2c color on a different index). It also emits multi-piece TeX constructions (long arrows, \mapsto, quotes, extensible brackets, brace fills) as one submobject (20 scenes). Measured on a clean Reference after fm-0v8k fixed its TeX cache race (Appendix C-22).

Native typesetting over bundled Computer Modern and fmd-math: glyph metrics and outlines differ from LaTeX by design. BN-05 keeps glyph order and count, and class/structure stays compared. Both engines set these in Computer Modern, so the box keeps the Reference's extent within 10% and its centre within 0.05 units.

Text, MarkupText and Code set bundled faces; the Reference sets whatever family its host maps through Pango (BN-05), so the Reference's own extent is a function of the host: Text('Hello') is 1.28 wide in the checked-in class-sweep facts and 1.049 on the differential host, where the portal's is 1.059. Envelope: extent within a quarter of the Reference's, centre within 0.05 units.
Glyph outlines inside text are BN-05 native typesetting. Glyph members align by index only, so their boxes are bounded through the text root's envelope.

Brace is a parametric path family, not a stretched \underbrace glyph render (BN-08 table). Its root is the drawn path, not a container of glyph children. A different outline, not a different size: the box stays within 10% of the Reference's extent and 0.05 units of its centre.
The Reference's brace glyph children do not exist in the parametric path family (BN-08).

DecimalNumber is native text through Scribe with a per-character glyph cache (BN-08, 'Why DecimalNumber is a cache'). Its digits are Computer Modern in both engines: extent within 10%, centre within 0.05 units.
Each digit is one glyph submobject, not a Text wrapping a glyph path, so the family is one level shallower (BN-08).

The Reference builds each Annulus circle with quadratic_bezier_points_for_arc(TAU), whose default is 8 components (35 points). FrankenManim applies BN-09's one arc-density rule, 16 components for a full circle (67 points). bbox stays compared.

Glyphs are VMobjectFromSVGPath since fm-15k9, but padding members that native family alignment creates during Scene.play are published as plain VMobject, while the Reference's invisible_copy keeps the source's class (one corpus scene: a Transform between Tex selections of different glyph counts).
The Reference's scene.mobjects starts with the CameraFrame; the portal's does not.

The portal's clock equals the Reference's segments counted by BN-02's rule, ceil(run_time * fps) on the exact f64 duration; the Reference's arange counts one frame fewer just above a frame boundary (wait(0.1) at 30 fps: 3 frames, BN-02 4).

De-TeX'd natives (BN-08 table): Checkmark/Exmark are drawn paths, Matrix brackets are drawn, BulletedList/Title set native text. The root is the drawn or native object, not a Tex glyph container. Drawn in place of a glyph, at the glyph's size: extent within 10%, centre within 0.05 units.
The Reference's Tex glyph children of these natives do not exist, or are native glyphs (BN-08).
C-15: the Reference's FunctionGraph declares color=YELLOW but never forwards it, so its graphs keep the default stroke. FrankenManim forwards it (BN-07).
One error-bounded cubic-to-quadratic converter for API cubics (BN-13). The Reference splits a cubic into two quadratics with no bound (5 points against 33).

A curved Arrow's stem edges use quadratic_bezier_points_for_arc(path_arc) at its default of 8 components in the Reference, and BN-09's one arc-density rule in FrankenManim. Fewer components move the quadratic handles, and so the bbox (6% of the height of Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, path_arc=PI / 2) in the class sweep). Straight arrows are equal. Envelope: extent within 10%, centre within 0.05 units.

Known metric bug past bn05-text-geometry's 10%: formulas run 2-18% narrow and fallback glyphs run wide (display integrals up to +35%, Tex('a + b') +23% from the '+'). The envelope states that magnitude, so a 2x Tex still fails. Since franken_markdown e4e8e2e (TeX's null delimiters around fractions) the construction set's Tex matches the Reference without this row, so it no longer covers constructions.
